Reaction-diffusion systems

Source: R/reaction-diffusion.R
reaction_diffusion_problem.Rd

reaction_diffusion_problem() defines a system of S species

Usage

reaction_diffusion_problem(
  mesh,
  species = "u",
  diffusion = 1,
  reaction,
  jacobian = NULL,
  initial,
  bcs = list(),
  time = c(0, 1),
  degree = 1
)

Arguments

mesh

A pde_mesh().

species

Character vector of species names.

diffusion

Diffusion coefficients: a number, or a list or vector with one entry (number or function(x, y)) per species.

reaction

function(u, x, y, t) where u is a matrix with one column per species (named) and one row per degree of freedom; it must return a matrix of the same shape.

jacobian

Optional function(u, x, y, t) returning an array of dimension c(n, S, S) with entries dR_a / du_b.

initial

A list with one initial condition per species.

bcs

A named list of boundary conditions per species; species without an entry get zero-flux conditions.

time

Start and end time.

degree

Lagrange degree.

Value

An object of class reaction_diffusion_problem.

Details

du_s/dt - div(D_s grad u_s) = R_s(u_1, ..., u_S, x, y, t), s = 1..S,

with per-species diffusion, initial conditions and boundary conditions.

The reaction term is discretized by the product (group finite-element) approximation: R is evaluated at the degrees of freedom, interpolated, and integrated against the test functions, giving M R(U). This is exact for linear reactions and second-order accurate in space for smooth nonlinear ones.

Time integration (argument method of solve_pde()):

  • "imex-euler": implicit diffusion, explicit reaction (first order); each species matrix is factored once.

  • "implicit-euler": fully implicit backward Euler with Newton's method on the coupled system and a backtracking line search. The reaction Jacobian is jacobian if given, otherwise computed by finite differences species by species (pointwise, so it is cheap and exact up to the difference error).

Positivity is not guaranteed by either scheme for general reactions.

Examples

mesh <- pde_mesh_rectangle(nx = 6)
prob <- reaction_diffusion_problem(
  mesh, species = "u", diffusion = 0.1,
  reaction = function(u, x, y, t) u * (1 - u),
  initial = list(u = function(x, y) 0.1 + 0.8 * x), time = c(0, 1))
sol <- solve_pde(prob, dt = 0.1)
